newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators seek adjustment in price index.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators seek adjustment in price index.

text.p: Eleven senators have written President Clinton reiterating their view that the Consumer Price Index should be adjusted down by one-half percentage point.

"Mainstream economists agree that the CPI is overstated from between 0.7 to two points and accordingly is not an accurate measure of inflation," the letter said. The adjustment would save $125 billion between fiscal 1997 and 2003, the letter said.
In the past, 46 members of the Senate have voted for a downward adjustment of the CPI, which would cut back the growth of mandatory spending pegged to inflation.

The ballooning growth of mandatory spending has steadily squeezed down the amount of money available for appropriated accounts. "Members of the Appropriations Committee understand the difficulties inherent in decreasing the amount of discretionary spending as a percentage of the budget each year," said the letter sent Friday, which was signed by Appropriations Committee Chairman Mark Hatfield, an Oregon Republican, and 10 others. They included Sen. Bob Kerrey, a Nebraska Democrat.
